findings.title: Unauthenticated PATCH /v1/connectors/{name}/tools re-enables ungated connector read tools
findings.description: The Connectors UI lets users disable individual tools (e.g. gmail_get_message) as a privacy control. PATCH /v1/connectors/{name}/tools accepts an arbitrary enabled map with no authentication beyond the localhost Origin gate, persists it via SecretStore profile {connector}:tools, and the next build_engine() includes those tools again. Connector tools with kind=read are classified approval_for_tool=False, so mailbox/CRM/calendar reads execute with no approval card.
findings.impact: Bypasses an intentional user privacy control. An attacker who can call the local sidecar can restore silent Gmail/HubSpot/Notion/GitHub read (and mis-kinded github_clone) capability for every new session, then drive the agent over WS or an allowlisted Slack mention to exfiltrate mail/CRM data into the transcript or a standing send_message target.
findings.attack_path: 1. Victim has gmail connected and disables gmail_get_message/gmail_search_messages in Settings. 2. Attacker (Origin http://localhost:* or missing Origin) PATCH /v1/connectors/gmail/tools with enabled map all true. 3. Attacker opens WS /ws/session/{new_id}?agent=cowork (or a new Slack @mention spawns a session) so build_engine runs _enabled_connector_tools against the patched flags. 4. user_message / inbound prompt causes gmail_search_messages + gmail_get_message — PermissionEngine treats them as low-risk reads (needs_user=False). 5. Message bodies appear in session events; on mention threads standing send_message can forward them outbound.
evidence: platform/coworker/agent.py:84-98 _enabled_connector_tools filters on tools[].enabled at engine build
findings.remediation: Require an explicit local capability token / CSRF secret for mutating connector policy routes. Treat tool enablement changes as consent-equivalent to connect. Consider requiring approval for previously user-disabled tools even when kind=read until the user re-enables them in the GUI.
findings.distinctness: Not Gmail filters/HubSpot hidden-fields (different privacy stores). Not allow/allow_deliver. Not inbox AUTO. Prior hunts dismissed PATCH tools as 'still needs approval' — that misses kind=read tools which never approve.

findings.title: Unauthenticated POST /v1/sessions/{id}/connections unmutes persona-muted connectors
findings.description: Session connection overrides let the GUI mute/unmute account-connected connectors per session. The REST writer is unauthenticated: posting enabled=true for a connector that the persona default muted makes effective_connectors include it again. New engines then register that connector's still-enabled tools, including ungated reads.
findings.impact: Bypasses the persona/session mute security layer. Restores full connector tool surface (subject to per-tool flags) for attacker-chosen sessions without re-consent.
findings.attack_path: 1. Persona defaults mute gmail (or user muted it for the session). 2. Attacker POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/connections {connector:gmail, enabled:true}. 3. Fresh engine for sid uses connector_filter=effective_connectors including gmail. 4. Drive ungated gmail_get_message / similar as in finding 1.
evidence: platform/coworker/connections.py:158-179 effective() session override wins over persona default
findings.remediation: Authenticate mutating session-connection writes the same way as other trust-boundary changes, or require a user-present confirmation token. Do not allow cross-origin localhost pages to flip mute state.
findings.distinctness: Different control plane from per-tool PATCH (persona/session mute vs tool enabled map). Prior near-miss called this mute-only with no credential plant — impact is privilege restoration of ungated reads, not credential theft.
